what: What METR prints about the 50 % time horizon on its Time Horizon 1.1 task suite, transcribed from the pinned post (metr.org/blog/2026-1-29-time-horizon-1-1, sha256 in meta.json) — nothing in this file is computed here. The ledger (certs/horizon-ledger.json) decides against it.

post.title: Time Horizon 1.1
post.method: for each model, a logistic regression of run success on log2(human minutes), runs weighted by task and by the inverse square root of the task family's size (figs.yaml: weighting invsqrt_task_weight, regularization 0.00001), the 50 % horizon read off the fitted curve; confidence intervals by bootstrapping over task families, tasks and runs; the doubling time from a trend of log2 horizon against release date over the models that were state of the art at release

all.th11Note: the stitched trend, TH1.0 estimates for pre-2023 models

table1.what: Table 'TH1 / TH1.1 / Change': the 50 % time horizon in minutes with the 95 % bootstrap interval, per model, on the two suites

table2.what: Table 'Vivaria / Inspect': five models run on the TH1 tasks on both infrastructures, minutes [95 % CI]

sentences.tighter: We increased the tasks in our suite by 34% (228/170) and doubled the number of tasks that are 8 hours or longer (31/14).
sentences.post2023: The post-2023 doubling-time is 131 days under TH1.1, compared to 165 days under TH1, meaning progress is estimated to be 20% more rapid under TH1.1.
sentences.post2024: We also report below the doubling time since 2024: this was at 109 days under TH1, and falls to 89 days under TH1.1.
sentences.shifts: estimates of recent models shifting up (GPT-5 and Opus 4.5 rise by 55% and 11% respectively)

repository.what: METR/eval-analysis-public at commit 52cb829 (2026-03-06): reports/time-horizon-1-1/data/raw/runs.jsonl (24,008 runs over 21 aliases, HCAST 15,176 · SWAA 8,287 · RE-Bench 545; score_binarized in {0, 1}; human_minutes 0.0199 to 1800; equal_task_weight and invsqrt_task_weight precomputed per alias), data/external/release_dates.yaml, reports/time-horizon-1-1/{params,fig_params/figs}.yaml. The pipeline's metrics outputs (logistic_fits/headline.yaml, agent_summary.csv) are DVC-tracked and NOT in git — the printed numbers above are the post's, and the post predates the repository's push by five weeks.
repository.estimator: src/horizon/utils/logistic.py: sklearn LogisticRegression(C = 1/regularization) with sample_weight (the chosen weight column, summing to 1 per agent), x = log2(human_minutes), y = score_binarized; horizon_p = 2^((logit p − intercept)/coef); src/horizon/compute_task_weights.py: equal_task_weight = 1/n_runs_in_task, invsqrt_task_weight = equal_task_weight / sqrt(n_tasks_in_family), each normalised to sum to 1 per agent

site.what: the live metr.org/time-horizons page (updated 2026-05-08): benchmark_results_1_1.yaml prints per model the p50/p80 estimate with a bootstrap interval and an is_sota flag; task_results_1_1.yaml prints per agent the fitted coefficient and intercept to three decimals and every task's minutes, successes, runs and weight
site.aliasToKeyNote: every other alias maps to its key by lowercasing and replacing non-alphanumerics with underscores; these five are the site's own renamings, transcribed

from_2023_on.note: excludes points with central estimate p50 > 16 hrs (the file's own comment)
